newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds mixed, peso bonds surge.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds mixed, peso bonds surge.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished mixed Wednesday with peso-denominated much higher and dollar bonds lower.
"There was big demand for peso bonds, above all from the U.S.," said a trader at a domestic bank.
The peso-denominated Bocon Proveedor 1 due 2007 surged 0.70 pesos to 100.30. Trade in peso bonds, once again, was much more busy than usual.
Investors upped their appetite for peso bonds first on Tuesday when Moody's rated Argentine peso debt B1, the same rating as foreign debt.
This sessions' announcement that Argentina has placed a 10-year, 500 million peso bond boosted peso bonds further. The bond was priced at 99.423 and carries a coupon of 11.75 percent.

But another trader said that the Argentine market is set to turn its focus back to the U.S. in coming sessions, considering the remaining U.S. indicators, including gross domestic product, due to be released this week.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.15 to 125.65, while the FRB Brady bond due 2005 fell 1/4 to 89.
Call money rates were unchanged at 5.20 percent.
